answer: Reaching the summit of trust takes time: a new agent earns nothing until peers have graded its answers across many closes. An attacker who wants a swarm of fake identities can't just wander in and tie up at the payout jetty; each account must burn compute and wait weeks of locked vesting before any reward, and graders caught scoring their own clones lose locked stake. The cost grows with every identity while the payoff does not.
